gates.label: Edge and provider capacity controls
gates.requirement: Provider-side CPU, storage, request, row, alarm, latency, and distributed-traffic evidence supports the published budget; the status and effect of the recommended path-scoped 48-per-10-second edge rule are recorded without treating it as an availability guarantee.
gates.currentEvidence: Deterministic source contracts bound per-visitor and global admission, lease lifetime, retry behavior, row lifecycle, and fail-closed provider errors. Under the public reusable testing token, however, one client can use the permitted 16-request acquisition sequence to fill all eight slots and renew them; the 48-per-10-second per-IP rule does not stop that sequence. The controls bound cost, state, and privacy consequence, not tool availability, and source cannot establish live provider capacity.
gates.evidenceNeeded: After deployment, record whether the recommended path-scoped edge rule is feasible and active, measure its actual effect, and perform a bounded production-representative exercise of CPU, storage, request, row, alarm, latency, distributed traffic, and public-token slot pressure. Retain observed abuse as a requalification trigger.
gates.rationale: Capacity failure and public-token slot starvation are plausible, but their consequence is bounded to demonstrator availability by fail-closed admission, eight-slot and lifetime caps, browser-local prose, and the absence of a paid overage path. The per-IP edge rule is moderate-value operational hardening, not a release prerequisite or complete answer to a reusable public token. Measuring the real provider and reopening on observed abuse has greater lifecycle value than claiming unavailable bot resistance.

A deliberately timed renewal trace has lower incremental value because extensive renewal contracts, bodyless PATCH requests, fail-closed client termination, bounded lease expiry, and eventual cleanup already constrain the plausible failure while an ordinary session can expose it without holding release completion.
